findings.title: Unguarded DB update inside catch can abort the whole batch
findings.body: The new `await prisma.workflowReminder.update(...)` in the catch block has no try/catch, and it is not inside any outer try. Before this PR the catch only logged, so it could not throw. Now, if this update fails, the exception escapes the `for` loop and the handler rejects. The most plausible trigger is a reminder deleted after `findMany` (for example when its booking is cancelled, which makes Prisma throw P2025), or any transient DB error. The consequence is that every remaining reminder in the batch is skipped for this cron run and the response is an error instead of the normal success response. The increment should be guarded so one bad row does not stop processing of the rest.

findings.title: retryCount delete branch is not scoped to SMS reminders
findings.body: The second branch of the `OR` (`retryCount: { gt: 1 }`) has no `method: WorkflowMethods.SMS` filter, unlike the first branch. Any WorkflowReminder of any method (EMAIL, WHATSAPP, or a future channel) with retryCount > 1 is deleted, regardless of its `scheduled` state. Only the SMS path increments the column today, so the practical impact is currently small, but the delete condition is broader than the stated intent and will cause data loss once another channel uses the column. The branch should be scoped as `method: WorkflowMethods.SMS` plus `retryCount: { gt: 1 }`.

findings.title: Comment describes only the date-based deletion
findings.body: The comment says this block deletes 'all scheduled sms reminders where scheduled date is past current date'. After this PR the same `deleteMany` also deletes reminders whose retryCount is greater than 1, including unscheduled ones that failed twice. The comment is now wrong and does not explain the retry threshold either.

findings.title: Reminders with no sendTo or empty message never accrue retries
findings.body: The retry increment only happens inside `if (message?.length && sendTo)` (the else branch at line 178 and the catch block). If `sendTo` is null (for example an SMS_ATTENDEE step where `booking.smsReminderNumber` is missing) or the message is empty, nothing is scheduled and retryCount is not incremented. Such a reminder stays unscheduled and is reprocessed on every cron run until its scheduledDate passes, with the template/DB work repeated each time. This is the 'keep retrying until the date is reached' behavior the PR is meant to stop, and the PR leaves this path uncovered. Either count these as failed attempts or delete them explicitly.

findings.title: Non-atomic read-modify-write of retryCount
findings.body: The counter is written as `reminder.retryCount + 1`, using the value read at the start of the run. If two cron invocations overlap (the job makes many external calls and can run long), both can read the same value and write the same increment, so failures are under-counted and a reminder gets an extra attempt. Prisma's `{ increment: 1 }` performs the increment atomically in the database and avoids this. The same pattern appears in the catch block at line 195.

findings.title: OR with an unindexed retryCount predicate forces a full table scan
findings.body: The new `OR` in deleteMany combines a predicate that uses the composite index `[method, scheduled, scheduledDate]` with `retryCount > 1`, which has no index (schema.prisma line 1000 adds the column without one). Postgres can only use a BitmapOr when every arm is indexable, so this cron query now falls back to a sequential scan of WorkflowReminder on every run. That table grows over time, so the cost increases with it. Consider an index on `retryCount` or splitting the delete into two queries.

findings.title: Retry budget of two attempts is spent within a few cron ticks with no backoff
findings.body: Each cron tick makes one attempt, and the row is deleted on the first tick after the second failure. Two failures can therefore occur only minutes apart, and a Twilio or network outage longer than that permanently drops the reminder with no log beyond a console line and no alert. The magic `gt: 1` also does not state the 'two failures' rule anywhere in code. The threshold or the lack of backoff should be a deliberate, documented choice.

findings.title: No tests for the new retry and deletion behavior
findings.body: The PR changes control flow in three places: failed scheduling increments retryCount, errors increment retryCount, and reminders with retryCount > 1 are deleted. None of this is covered by a test in the diff. A test that drives the handler with a mocked twilio.scheduleSMS returning null or throwing, and checks the retryCount updates and the deletion on the next run, would catch regressions such as the catch-block issue above.
